correctness.rationale: Exact uniform-shell propagation yields a Markov chain with independent geometric resets; coupling with the same signs gives a deterministic bound by maximum reset mark and an Np2^-d tail. For p>1/2 a negative-drift Foster criterion and ergodic renewal frequency make the maximum mark asymptotic to log_2 N a.s. In the triangular critical window, centered Bernoulli increments obey Donsker, Skorokhod reflection is continuous, and the maximal coupling error is o_P(sqrt N). Brownian level sets of a fixed a have zero time measure, yielding the deep-shell occupation convergence and the explicit mean by Gaussian integration. Actual checker.py path was executed and passed; finite tests are only corroboration.

originality.rationale: Published papers give the exact dyadic shell chain, the binary auxiliary reflected-walk description, stationary and transient observables; these are credited as premises. The new theorem quantitatively couples the actual shell process to a SAME-CHOICES reflected walk with an all-horizon geometric maximum tail and proves its optimal almost-sure logarithmic order for fixed supercritical probability. This sharp bound transfers the WHOLE near-critical process and deep-shell time occupation to reflected Brownian motion; no matching or stronger physical-depth maximum-coupling/occupation theorem was identified in reviewed same-object sources. Novelty is qualified by residual risk of equivalent strong approximations in wider probability literature.
residual_risks: The Monthus binary representation and classical reflection theorem make this a close literature-implication case; a stronger unpublished strong-approximation theorem might cover it.

value.rationale: A quantified finite-horizon coupling gives an actionable pathwise replacement of nonlinear interval dynamics by the simplest reflected walk, and its error exponent is sharp. The whole-process critical-window limit provides a natural description of intermittency in exponentially tiny physical populations, while the nondegenerate deep-shell occupancy statistic makes the failure of deterministic time-average behavior quantitative. These are not merely finite enumeration or an arbitrary parameter slice; the critical window is picked by the zero Lyapunov exponent and the sqrt N random-walk scale.
